# THE RITE AND THE WORKSHOP

*The line every surface built so far has held in its own words, collected in
one place before a console has to hold it centrally. Nothing new is ruled here.
What is new is only that the line is now written once instead of six times.*

## I · TWO HANDS, FOUR SURFACES

The portal's surfaces divide, and the division is not stylistic.

A **rite** takes chance, commits it, and answers a question that a person
brought. It lives under [the Caster's Law](../LUMINARA_CASTERS_LAW.md): the
chance is unsteerable, committed and witnessable, and the reading refuses
operation, prediction and authority.

A **workshop** takes no chance and answers no question. It shows structure that
was already true before anyone opened it, and it would show the same structure
to an empty room.

Placed against the two substrates, the four built surfaces fill a lattice with
no gaps and no duplicates:

|  | rite | workshop |
|---|---|---|
| **cube** | the Living Cube | the Cube Lens |
| **torus** | the Wayfinder | the Sea |

## II · WHAT ALREADY RULES EACH SIDE, COLLECTED

The rite side has one law and it is written: the Caster's Law, in full.

The workshop side has no single law, and instead holds the line in six places,
each in its own words:

- **The cymatics bench**, sealed 2026-07-16: *"the bench is the INSTRUMENT, not
  the reading... no cymatic layer joins a reading without a further ruling."*
- **The Sea**, whose pins assert on the page's own source that nothing there is
  a reading, that no fresh entropy exists in the file, and that no casting
  function may be imported.
- **The Cube Lens**, carrying the same assertion and the same pins.
- **The letter table**, which shows an open question without ever seating an
  answer.
- **[The law of spreads](THE_LAW_OF_SPREADS.md)**, parking the 729 at the point
  where derivation would end and authorship would begin.
- **[The holding](../THE_HOLDING_PLAN.md)**, whose sketch refuses to accept a
  question at the start, on the grounds that a question at the start plus a
  card at the end is a reading wearing a game's clothes.

Six statements of one line. Every instrument built so far has held it
independently, which is the strongest evidence that the line is real: nobody
was enforcing it centrally and nobody crossed it.

## III · THE TWO CROSSINGS THAT BREAK LAW

A console is the first thing that would carry both hands at once, so the
crossings become mechanical rather than hypothetical. There are exactly two,
and they are symmetric.

**A workshop may not steer a cast.** This is not a new rule; it is the first
word of the Caster's Law applied. The chance is UNSTEERABLE, and *"what kills
divination is not bias but steerability."* A workshop that could seed, nudge,
re-roll or supply entropy to a rite would be a steering mechanism whatever it
was called. Concretely: no workshop surface offers a cast, and no state a
workshop holds may reach the entropy that a cast consumes.

**A cast may not enter a workshop.** This one is ruled in a single instance
rather than generally: the cymatics ruling forbids that instrument joining a
reading without a further ruling. Whether that generalises to every instrument
is a canon act and is not taken here. What can be said without deciding it is
that **every instrument so far has behaved as though it generalises**, and that
the failure mode is specific: a workshop showing structure about a person's own
cast is no longer showing structure that was true before they opened it. It has
become an interpretive layer on a rite, and it would arrive there without
anyone choosing it.

## IV · WHAT CROSSES FREELY

Everything that is true regardless of who is looking.

A **card** crosses. It is one of twenty-seven, letter-free, meaning nothing on
its own.

A **dyad**, a **line**, a **plane**, a **diagonal**, a **shell** all cross.
They are canon structure, derived, and were true before the console existed.

A **seed**, replayed rather than drawn, crosses in one direction only: the Sea
already replays a declared, already-committed cast without being a caster, and
its pins hold that shape exactly. Replay is not chance.

The distinction throughout is simple to state and easy to check: **structure
crosses, situations do not.**

## V · THE MECHANIC THIS GIVES A CONSOLE

Three consequences, offered as architecture rather than as law.

**The card is the invariant; a mode is a projection.** Every card already has a
code, a knot, a cube position, a torus winding and a place on the wheel, all
derived. So a console holds one focus and each mode draws it. Nothing needs
translating between modes because nothing was ever in a mode to begin with.

**Focus crosses a mode switch; a cast does not.** Move from the Wayfinder to
the Lens and the card being looked at comes with you. The reading does not.
That single rule implements section III without needing a guard anywhere else.

**No workshop surface may hold a caster.** The absence is the safeguard. It is
also already how all four surfaces are built, so this costs nothing to adopt
and would cost a great deal to lose by accident.

## PROVENANCE

*Written 26 July 2026 at the architect's word, before beginning the synthesis
of the instruments, on the reasoning that a console merging four surfaces
across this line is exactly where six scattered rulings could be reconciled
into one wrong one. Nothing here is newly ruled. The Caster's Law and the six
workshop statements are quoted or cited as they stand; the first crossing is an
application of the law's own opening word; the second is explicitly left as an
open canon act, with only the observed pattern recorded. The lattice in section
I was found rather than designed, across four surfaces built at different times
for unrelated reasons. Letter-free.*
